newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed but mood bearish.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed but mood bearish.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Tuesday after support levels held following a sharp sell off in the past week.
While some short covering is expected ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving Holiday Thursday, the market remains bearish and could yet slide lower, traders said.
"The market looks oversold and a bounce was expected today, but it didn't really happen, leaving many people a bit scared," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
COMEX February gold ended up 60 cents at $376.80, after barely holding above contract lows seen Monday at $375.10.

Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $374.70/375.20, after gold was fixed in London Tuesday afternoon at $373.50, its lowest fix since January 9, 1995. Spot gold closed around $374.50/90 in New York Monday.
COMEX March silver closed down 0.3 cent at $4.785 an ounce, holding above Monday's lows at $4.755.
With Wednesday being first notice day for December gold and silver, the focus was again on the roll out of the December contracts, traders said.
Also in traders minds was the U.S. Thanksgiving Holiday which will close both COMEX and NYMEX Thursday and Friday.
February is now the most active nearby contract in COMEX gold futures, after a sharp jump in February gold's open interest to 73,412 contracts Monday.
The December/February spread widened to $2.10 an ounce Tuesday, after narrowing steadily from around $2.80 in July.

On the charts, February gold remains in its downtrend since at least mid-October, but has again neared oversold levels around 20 pct on a standard nine-day relative strength index (RSI), analysts noted.
But fundamentals remains bearish for gold in particular, analysts said.

Commodity funds continue to hold record net short positions in COMEX gold futures, while U.S. stock and bond markets continue their rally, providing little incentive for investment in gold, analysts said.

Concern about European central bank gold sales has also been revived in the past few days by reports Switzerland may be going to change its constitution to take the country off its quasi-gold standard which requires gold reserves to be held equal to 40 pct of its currency in circulation.
The spot gold/silver ratio recovered further to 79.05 Tuesday from a four week low at 76.69 on November 20, as silver remained the weaker commodity.
COMEX March silver, which saw a contract low at $4.755 an ounce Monday, is now the most active silver contract with open interest of 47,380 contracts Monday.
In the bullion market spot silver held around $4.75 an ounce Tuesday, after trading down to a four week low at $4.70 Monday.
NYMEX January platinum closed up 70 cents at $382.70 an ounce, after holding just above the contract low at $381.00 seen Monday.
NYMEX March palladium, now the active contract, ended down 10 cents at $117.50.
The April 1997 platinum/April 1997 gold spread narrowed for the third day in a row, ending around $6.00 an ounce, down from a high of $9.40 on November 21.
-- Clive McKeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
